record.title: Fold2Seq: A Joint Sequence(1D)-Fold(3D) Embedding-based Generative Model for Protein Design
record.reason: Include: Fold2Seq is specifically protein-sequence design conditioned on folds. Experiments use CATH structures with separate seen-fold and unseen-fold splits, Tables1–2 assess sequence recovery and diversity, and Figure3 compares predicted structural recovery against RosettaDesign. Additional challenges study low-resolution, missing-residue and NMR-ensemble inputs. Results are computational protein-design validation, not wet-lab or clinical efficacy.

record.title: Marginal Contribution Feature Importance - an Axiomatic Approach for Explaining Data
record.reason: Include: Main Sections5.3–5.4 substantively evaluate feature importance using BRCA gene-expression data from571 patients and EHRs of7889 bloodstream-infection patients. BRCA experiments compare known cancer-gene ranking and stability under added genes; mortality experiments examine removal of RBC-correlated blood measures, with predictive AUC0.80/0.78. Main real applications are biomedical; synthetic tests and supplementary UCI feature-duplication robustness are secondary. Associations and predictive importance do not establish causal biomarkers.

record.title: Disentangling syntax and semantics in the brain with deep networks
record.reason: Include: Sections3.2–3.3 and5 map factorized GPT-2 representations to averaged fMRI responses from345 listeners. Held-out narrative intervals, phonological controls and multiple-comparison-corrected regional analyses support a shared distributed syntactic/semantic substrate and broader compositional recruitment. Figures5–6 report neural encoding results. This is basic human language neuroscience, without diagnostic or treatment claims.
